changes.why: v0.14.0 removed R.charAt, deprecated in v0.12.0 for nthChar
v0.14.0 removed R.charCodeAt, deprecated in v0.12.0 for nthCharCode
v0.14.0 makes every where spec value a predicate and moves the value entries to the new whereEq, so the support datatype for a function-or-value spec entry encodes nothing and is removed

v0.14.0's where calls every spec value as a predicate with the test object's property alone, undefined when absent (a value entry throws; where({a: x => x === undefined}, {}) went from false to true): the signature changed from map<string, SpecVal<V>> to map<string, Option<V> -> bool>

v0.14.0 pushes each kept element again (out[out.length], f5966efd), so no holes are left (differenceWith(eq, [1, 2, 3, 4], [2]) went from [1, <hole>, 3, 4] to [1, 3, 4]): the kept-prefix precondition is dropped, with every result inside it unchanged

v0.14.0's drop is n <= 0 ? list : _slice(list, n) ("treat negative number as zero"): n widens from nat to int and a negative n gives the list (drop(-1, [1, 2]) went from [undefined, 1, 2] to [1, 2]), with every result for n >= 0 unchanged
new in v0.14.0 (@category List): adjust(fn, idx, list) applies fn to the element at idx, a negative idx counting from the end; out of range the list
new in v0.14.0 (@category List): update(idx, x, list) is adjust(always(x), idx, list)
new in v0.14.0 (@category List): intersperse(separator, list) puts the separator between the elements
new in v0.14.0 (@category List): dropRepeatsWith(pred, list) keeps the first element and each element pred does not match with the last one kept
new in v0.14.0 (@category List): dropRepeats is dropRepeatsWith with Object.is
new in v0.14.0 (@category List): lensIndex(n) is lens(nth(n), set by _slice cuts); the getter requires the index in the list and the setter n >= -1
new in v0.14.0 (@category Object): lensProp(k) is lens(prop(k), assoc(k)); the getter requires the key
new in v0.14.0 (@category Object): whereEq(spec, testObj) is where(mapObj(eq, spec), testObj), where's former value entries
new in v0.14.0 (@category Function): composeL composes lenses right to left (binary here)
new in v0.14.0 (@category Function): pipeL composes lenses left to right, composeL of the reversed lenses (binary here)
new in v0.14.0 (@category Math): mean(list) is sum(list) / list.length, a real; NaN for [], so the list must not be empty
new in v0.14.0 (@category Math): median(list) is the mean of the middle one or two elements of the sorted list; NaN for [], so the list must not be empty
